html:
SMTO-GML-0002 — Your Gmail account changed while SMTO was using it

GUID: 8362bfa7-57b7-426c-9e91-a757667c2a22
Slug: gmail-account-changed
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • The saved Gmail account was edited, reconnected, renamed or removed after this request started using it. SMTO stopped so it wouldn't keep working with outdated account details.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open More options › Parameter Store, find the Gmail account, and make sure it still exists and shows the email address you expect. The account entry may have been edited, replaced or deleted while the task was running.
  2. Check Gmail for anything the earlier request already did, such as sent emails or moved messages. Work finished before the change stays done, so checking prevents doing it twice.
  3. Start a new request and mention the account with @ so SMTO uses its current details. SMTO only continues with account details that haven't changed since the request began.
  4. If you were connecting Gmail through a Google sign-in, start the connection again and don't edit the account entry until it finishes. The sign-in is tied to the account as it was when the connection started.

What success looks like

  • The new request runs with the account you mentioned and finishes without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Avoid editing a Gmail account entry while a task that uses it is still running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gmail account or its OAuth app record changed (revision, creation time or identity) between when the request bound it and when it was used, during token saving, accepted @ reference resolution, or app-password continuation.

What this means

  • Token saving finds changed/deleted account creation or update revision, or a changed OAuth app revision; accepted-account resolution can likewise detect changed identity. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Token saving finds changed/deleted account creation or update revision, or a changed OAuth app revision; accepted-account resolution can likewise detect changed identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the captured key, revisions and account/app identity before saving new tokens.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the account mapping in Parameter Store and confirm the intended identity (email, oauth_app_ref, creation and update revisions). Start a fresh request or connect flow bound to the current record; do not resubmit a stale account reference, and reconcile any work already recorded in receipts before repeating it.
  • Refresh the account mapping and confirm the intended identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A fresh supported flow binds the intended unchanged account/app revision.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
